title: Tightness of Post-Quantum Bounds for Ascon and Keyed Sponges
summary: The current post-quantum analysis of Ascon, IKS, FKS, OKS, and KMAC is capped by (tweakable) Even–Mansour bounds; find matching attacks or establish stronger bounds by another technique.

formal_statement.body: For Ascon and the keyed sponge functions $\mathrm{IKS}$, $\mathrm{FKS}$, $\mathrm{OKS}$, and $\mathrm{KMAC}$ in the post-quantum setting, determine whether attacks can match their existing security bounds or, alternatively, establish stronger bounds using a different technique. The current approach is capped by the security bounds for (tweakable) Even--Mansour; no matching attacks are known, and the existing bounds are expected not to be tight.

scope.domain: Post-quantum cryptanalysis of Ascon and the keyed sponge functions IKS, FKS, OKS, and KMAC.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Find attacks matching the existing security bounds or establish stronger bounds using a different technique.

citations.label: Post-Quantum Security of Keyed Sponge-Based Constructions through a Modular Approach

progress.summary: In its limitations and future-work discussion, the source says the current approach inherits a cap from (tweakable) Even–Mansour security bounds. It reports no matching attacks and expects the resulting bounds not to be tight.
